study.title: GP-26-01 Sentinel Patch Evaluation
study.background: Postoperative pain and recovery are often assessed at irregular intervals, limiting the ability to describe recovery between clinic visits. This prospective observational study evaluates whether a wearable Sentinel Patch can support structured symptom and device-use follow-up.
study.hypothesis: Structured monitoring will provide a complete and operationally usable record of postoperative recovery through Month 3.

objectives.primary: To describe the change in postoperative pain score from baseline to Month 3.
objectives.secondary: To describe device adherence, usability, and the frequency of safety events during follow-up.

population.study_population: Approximately 60 adults 18 to 80 years of age will be enrolled across two investigational sites.
inclusion_criteria: Eligible historical postoperative records are available for abstraction.
Able and willing to complete prospective Sentinel Patch follow-up through Month 3.
exclusion_criteria: Concurrent participation in an interventional study.
Historical records are incomplete for the planned abstraction.
population.sample_justification: The sample is intended to provide descriptive estimates of pain recovery, adherence, usability, and safety while allowing for expected attrition through Month 3.

design.study_design: Prospective, multicenter, single-arm observational study with historical record abstraction and prospective Sentinel Patch monitoring.

procedures.assessments: Historical chart abstraction, baseline enrollment, Month 1 telephone follow-up, and Month 3 clinic follow-up, including pain score review, device-use download, and usability questionnaire.
procedures.methods: The same approved assessment schedule will be used at both sites. Historical and prospective observations will be labeled by source and visit.
procedures.consent: Written informed consent will be obtained before any study-specific prospective procedure. Permission for historical record abstraction will be documented in the same consent process.
procedures.visit_schedule: Participants will complete screening and baseline activities before device initiation, a Month 1 telephone follow-up within the stated window, and a Month 3 clinic follow-up within the stated window.
procedures.assessment_details: At each applicable contact, the study team will review pain score, device use, adverse events, concomitant concerns, and completion of the relevant case report form.
procedures.unscheduled_visits: Unscheduled contacts may be performed when needed to address a safety concern, device issue, or missing assessment and will be recorded with the reason and outcome.
procedures.discontinued_subjects: Participants may discontinue at any time. The investigator will document the reason when available and retain data collected before discontinuation as permitted by consent and applicable requirements.
procedures.retention: The study team will use reminder calls and scheduled follow-up contacts to support completion through Month 3.
procedures.discontinuation: A participant may stop device use or withdraw from prospective follow-up without penalty or loss of entitled care.
procedures.termination: The investigator may terminate participation for a safety concern, protocol noncompliance, inability to complete follow-up, or loss to follow-up.
procedures.study_termination: The sponsor or investigator may terminate the study for safety, feasibility, regulatory, or operational reasons.
procedures.study_completion: The study is complete after the final enrolled participant has completed or discontinued Month 3 follow-up and required closeout activities are documented.

statistics.analysis_plan: The primary analysis will summarize change in pain score from baseline to Month 3. Secondary analyses will summarize adherence, usability responses, and adverse events using descriptive statistics.
statistics.methodology: Continuous variables will be summarized using count, mean, standard deviation, median, and range as appropriate. Categorical variables will be summarized using counts and percentages.
statistics.software: Analyses will be performed using validated statistical software under the sponsor's data-management procedures.

safety.general_information: The investigator will review safety information at every study contact and will ensure that relevant events are documented in the case report form.
safety.monitoring: Participants will be asked about adverse events, device-related complaints, and changes in health status at each scheduled contact.
safety.adverse_events: Adverse events and serious adverse events will be recorded from consent through the end of study participation, assessed for severity and relationship, and reported according to applicable requirements.
safety.follow_up: The investigator will follow unresolved adverse events and quality complaints until resolution, stabilization, or documentation that further follow-up is not clinically meaningful.

ethics.considerations: The study will be conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki, ICH GCP, the approved protocol, informed consent requirements, and applicable regulations.
ethics.confidentiality: Study records will use coded identifiers. Access to identifiable information will be limited to authorized study personnel and oversight bodies as permitted by law.

confidentiality.publication: Study results may be presented or published in a manner that does not identify individual participants.
confidentiality.data_handling: Data will be stored in access-controlled study systems and retained according to the approved record-retention plan.

risks_benefits.risks: Risks are expected to be minimal. Historical record review creates a confidentiality risk. Prospective patch use may cause temporary skin irritation, redness, itching, adhesive sensitivity, or discomfort. Participants may experience inconvenience from follow-up contacts, questionnaires, clinic attendance, or device-use activities.
risks_benefits.benefits: Participants may not receive a direct benefit. The study may improve understanding of postoperative recovery and the operational use of structured wearable monitoring.
risks_benefits.compensation_or_reimbursement: Any reimbursement will be described in the approved informed consent materials and administered according to site procedures.
risks_benefits.injury_handling: Study-related injuries will receive appropriate medical evaluation and treatment. The investigator will document and report suspected study-related injury according to applicable requirements.

endpoints.primary: Change in postoperative pain score from baseline to Month 3.

protocol.introduction: This protocol describes the approved objectives, population, procedures, operational safeguards, and analysis plan for GP-26-01.
protocol.objectivesIntro: The study objectives are evaluated using the scheduled historical and prospective assessments.
protocol.populationLong: The study will enroll approximately 60 adults across two sites. Participants must have eligible historical records and be able to complete the prospective Sentinel Patch schedule.
protocol.studyDesignLong: This is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm observational study combining historical chart abstraction with prospective monitoring.
protocol.methods: Standardized visit windows, source labels, and case report forms will be used to reduce collection variability.
protocol.studyProcedure: Study procedures include consent, historical abstraction, baseline assessment, device monitoring, Month 1 telephone follow-up, and Month 3 clinic follow-up.
protocol.consent: Consent will be obtained before study-specific prospective procedures and historical record abstraction.
protocol.visitScheduleDetails: The Schedule of Assessments defines the required visit names, windows, and CRF identifiers.
protocol.measurementsDetails: Pain score, device use, usability, adverse events, and relevant clinical information will be collected at applicable visits.
protocol.analysisDataSets: The analysis sets will include enrolled participants with available baseline and follow-up data, with exclusions documented in the analysis report.
protocol.statisticalMethodology: Descriptive statistics will be used for the primary and secondary objectives.
protocol.statisticalConsiderations: Missing data and participant discontinuation will be summarized and considered when interpreting results.
protocol.sampleSizeJustification: The planned sample supports descriptive estimation while allowing for expected attrition.
protocol.confidentialityPublication: Results will be reported in aggregate and without participant identifiers.
protocol.risks: The expected risks are minimal and include confidentiality risk, temporary skin effects, and inconvenience.
protocol.benefits: The study may contribute useful evidence about structured postoperative monitoring.
protocol.ethics: The study will follow approved ethical and regulatory requirements.
protocol.ethicalConfidentiality: Participant confidentiality will be protected through coded identifiers and access controls.
protocol.measurements: Standard evaluation procedures include pain, device-use, usability, and safety assessments.
protocol.confidentiality: Study data will be handled using approved access, retention, and publication controls.
protocol.injury_compensation: Injury evaluation and any reimbursement will follow the approved consent and site procedures.
protocol.endpointCriteria: Study endpoints are based on completion or discontinuation of the approved follow-up schedule.
protocol.completion: Completion is assessed after the Month 3 visit or documented final contact.
protocol.discontinuation: Participants may discontinue without penalty, with the reason and available data documented.
protocol.termination: Participation may be terminated for safety, noncompliance, inability to complete follow-up, or loss to follow-up.
protocol.studyTermination: The study may be terminated for safety, regulatory, feasibility, or operational reasons.
protocol.studyCompletion: Study completion occurs after final participant follow-up and closeout documentation.
